node.title: Summary — When the Controls Work but the System Fails
node.reading:
This summary is based on the public-facing article written by Iv án Abril Palma, which explains the foundations and gives a full account of the work. Full article: a public-facing explanation of the foundations

The contribution-and-limits appendix identifies what the current artifacts establish. For each system-level statement, locate the supporting object and the condition a test could challenge. A concise explanation should preserve the distinction between a proposed mechanism, a constructed scenario and an outcome independently reproduced.

Institutional context. The ITU-T Focus Group on Trust and Identity for Humans and Agentic AI (FG-TIDA) was announced by the International Telecommunication Union at the AI for Good Global Summit on 9 July 2026 and reports to ITU-T Study Group 17. The Integral Management Society contributes to this open pre-standardization work. Ecosystem Awareness is our association’s independently developed contribution to that wider field; publication here does not imply endorsement by ITU, AI for Good or FG-TIDA.

Our association, The Integral Management Society, is contributing six anti-goals as a model to the open work of FG-TIDA, an ITU-T focus group: what must a system preserve to avoid global failures even when its local controls keep working?

A multinational automates its work with AI: it consumes 100 million tokens and creates an enormous burden of human supervision. In the end, no substantive work is completed and no useful new information is produced.
